roles.look: the grumpy old Texan rancher with a cream straw cowboy hat, bushy silver eyebrows, a silver handlebar mustache, a faded blue denim shirt and a plum bandana
the upbeat young creator with caramel-blonde curls in a messy bun, freckles, a butter-yellow cropped hoodie, light jeans and small gold hoop earrings

beats.text: Together: We listen and we don’t judge
Face cream on his boots. Josie’s side-eye says everything.
His hat is a costume-shop replacement. Earl silently seethes.
No judgment. Two painfully fake smiles.

shots.prompt: Use the provided image as the first frame. Preserve the beautiful tactile 3D animated character designs and clothing. Soft neutral daylight, believable skin and fabric colors, restrained saturation, no orange wash. Stable eye-level medium two-shot, both faces always fully visible; Earl on the left, Josie on the right, on the same sofa. Comedy comes from tiny involuntary facial reactions followed by painfully forced politeness. No cuts within this take, no subtitles, no added people, no background music; quiet room tone. {Lead} sits left; {Partner} sits right. 0–2.5 seconds: both look at the camera and say together, "We listen and we don't judge." 2.5–6 seconds: Lead casually confesses, "I polish my boots with your face cream." Partner silently freezes; her smile drops, one eyebrow climbs, her eyes flick down to his boots and back at his face in horrified disbelief. 6–8 seconds: hold on her silent side-eye. She presses her lips together, takes a tiny breath and forces an impossibly tight polite smile. 8–10 seconds: Partner says through that strained smile, "No judgment." Lead notices her face, raises an innocent eyebrow. Only the assigned character speaks each line. The reaction is judgmental, never angry yelling; neither admits judging.

This is the second confession in the same conversation. 0–5.5 seconds: Partner cheerfully confesses, "I sold your real hat. That one's from a costume shop." Lead goes utterly still. His bushy eyebrows slowly pinch together; he looks up at his own hat brim, touches it with two fingers, then gives her a long wounded, accusing side-eye. 5.5–8 seconds: Partner studies his expression with an innocent smile. Lead starts to object without speaking, stops himself, swallows and forces a rigid smile. 8–10 seconds: Lead says very slowly and tightly, "No judgment." Partner gives a tiny smug nod. End on both staring sideways at each other while holding painfully fake polite smiles. No laughing away the tension; neither admits judging. Only the assigned speaker moves their lips for each line.

voiceProfiles.earl: Low baritone with a dry, weathered texture and a gentle Texas drawl. Unhurried, understated delivery; short skeptical pauses and clipped deadpan punchlines. Warm beneath the grumbling. Never a booming announcer or exaggerated cowboy caricature.
voiceProfiles.josie: Bright, warm mid-high voice with lightly breathy texture and conversational American English. Quick, playful phrasing and an audible smile; sincerity turns into mischievous restraint. Natural adult speech, never squeaky or a commercial presenter.
